assumptions: HYPOTHESIS: line parameters shared by actual affine EC witnesses correlate with downstream degree-four closure conflicts.
MODEL-BOUND: the signal, if present, may depend on the chosen short-Weierstrass coordinate chart.
HEURISTIC: 31 domain-separated within-class hash rankings provide a useful finite null distribution but not a random-oracle theorem.
UNTESTED: any retained-support gain can later be compiled without losing it to advice, optimizer, or target-descent costs.
falsification_conditions: The secant compiler fails to exceed the empirical 95th percentile of 31 matched hash compilers on every valid curve.
Almost every nonidentity two-sum output has a singleton witness class, making the compilers effectively identical.
The candidate violates injectivity, associativity, unique factorization, acyclicity, final-edge exclusion, or exact witness lift.
Independent verification fails to reproduce a curve, factor base, witness class, representative, conflict graph, optimizer certificate, or retained support.
interpretation_limits: Three seven-bit curves cannot establish asymptotic scaling.
A representative-selection signal is not relation generation or an index-calculus algorithm.
A gain may be coordinate-chart specific and must later survive admissible coordinate rescaling.
The experiment does not measure relation-matrix rank, linear algebra, individual logarithms, or an end-to-end rho comparison.
Novelty remains unverified pending a dedicated literature review.
hypothesis.mechanism: For each nonidentity point R in 2F, choose its unordered witness pair by lexicographically minimizing the actual affine line parameters (lambda, nu) before source indices. This may align recursive compositions and reduce forced degree-four closure conflicts while preserving the exact two-sum output classes and their multiplicities.
